title: Gravitational fields & potential
examples: How does the strength of the gravitational field change with distance?
What is the difference between gravitational force and gravitational potential?
Can you show me an example of gravitational field lines?

explain.say: Today we explore gravitational fields and potential energy. We will look at how gravity changes with distance.
The strength of the gravitational field, we call it g, depends on the mass and distance. Specifically, g equals G times M divided by r squared.
Next we look at gravitational potential. Potential energy is the stored energy due to position in a field. It is a scalar quantity.
Gravitational field lines help us visualize the field's strength and direction. The lines point from higher to lower potential.
When an object moves in a field, the change in potential energy is related to the work done by the gravitational force. This change is negative when moving away from the mass.
Consider a satellite orbiting a planet. As it moves higher, its gravitational potential energy decreases. This is an everyday example of potential change.

faq.q: What is the difference between force and potential?
faq.a: Force is a vector that tells you the push or pull at a point. Potential is a scalar that tells you the stored energy at a point.
asks: Are force and potential the same thing?

faq.q: Does the strength of gravity change if I move far away?
faq.a: Yes, the strength decreases with the square of the distance. This is described by the inverse square law.
asks: How does gravity change with distance?
Is gravity stronger closer to the mass?

faq.q: What do the field lines actually show?
faq.a: The field lines show the direction and strength of the gravitational field. They point inwards towards the massive object.
asks: What is the meaning of field lines?
Do field lines show force or potential?

faq.q: Why is the change in potential energy negative when moving out?
faq.a: Because the gravitational force does negative work when you move away from the mass. You are doing work against the field.
asks: Does energy increase or decrease when moving away?

faq.q: Can I use this concept for electricity too?
faq.a: Yes, the concepts are very similar. Electricity has electric fields and electric potential energy. The math structure is analogous.
asks: Does this apply to other forces?

facts: The gravitational field strength g follows an inverse square law.
Gravitational potential energy (U) is a scalar quantity.
Field lines point from regions of higher to lower potential.
The relationship is g = G M / r².

quiz.say: If you double the distance from a mass, how does the field strength change?

options.show: It becomes four times the original strength.
options.say: It becomes four times the original strength.

options.show: It becomes one quarter of the original strength.
options.say: It becomes one quarter of the original strength.

options.show: It becomes one half of the original strength.
options.say: It becomes one half of the original strength.

quiz.why: Because the relationship is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, doubling the distance divides the strength by four.

wrong.0: This would mean the force is constant regardless of distance.
wrong.1: This confuses the inverse square law with a direct square relationship.
wrong.3: This would suggest a direct inverse relationship, like g ∝ 1/r.

quiz.say: When lifting a mass against gravity, what happens to its potential energy?

options.show: The potential energy stays the same.
options.say: The potential energy stays the same.

options.show: It depends on the mass only.
options.say: It depends on the mass only.

quiz.why: Doing positive work against a conservative force like gravity increases the stored potential energy.

wrong.1: This would happen if gravity was doing the work on the mass.
wrong.2: This would imply no change in height or position.
wrong.3: Potential energy also depends on the change in height or position.

quiz.say: If a field line is drawn perpendicular to the radius vector, what does this imply?

options.show: The potential is at a local maximum or minimum.
options.say: The potential is at a local maximum or minimum.

options.show: The object is moving at constant velocity.
options.say: The object is moving at constant velocity.

options.show: The potential energy is constant everywhere.
options.say: The potential energy is constant everywhere.

quiz.why: When the field line is perpendicular to the radial line, the change in potential with distance is zero, indicating an extremum.

wrong.1: Zero force means no field line, not just a perpendicular line.
wrong.2: This relates to mechanics, not the field geometry itself.
wrong.3: Constant potential would mean no field lines are present.
